## My commitment to accessibility

I believe that the web should be accessible to everyone, regardless of their abilities or the technology they use. This site has been built with accessibility as a core principle, and I'm committed to maintaining and improving its accessibility over time.

If you encounter any accessibility barriers while using this site or accessing my content, please [contact me](/contact) and let me know. I'll do my best to address the issue promptly.

---

## Accessibility features

This site implements the following accessibility practices:

### Visual design
- **WCAG 2.1 Level AA compliant color contrast** — All text meets minimum contrast ratios (at least 4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text)
- **Dark and light mode support** — Choose your preferred color scheme based on your needs and preferences
- **Readable typography** — The site uses **Commissioner** (body text) and **Fraunces** (headings), both designed for clarity and readability across all users, including those with dyslexia or low vision
- **Sufficient spacing and sizing** — Text, buttons, and interactive elements are sized and spaced for easy interaction and reading

### Navigation and interaction
- **Keyboard navigation** — All interactive elements are fully navigable using only the keyboard (Tab, Enter, Escape keys)
- **Visible focus indicators** — When using keyboard navigation, focused elements are clearly indicated with visible borders or outlines
- **Semantic HTML** — The site uses proper heading hierarchy and semantic elements for better screen reader navigation
- **Descriptive link text** — Links use clear, descriptive text that makes sense out of context
- **Form accessibility** — Contact forms include associated labels and clear instructions

### Content and media
- **Alternative text for images** — All informative images include descriptive alt text for screen reader users
- **Video captions** — External video content includes captions where available
- **Table of contents** — Blog posts include a navigable table of contents for easier browsing

### Technical standards
- **Mobile responsive** — The site works well on all screen sizes from phones to large displays
- **Screen reader compatible** — Built with semantic HTML and ARIA labels where needed for assistive technology users
- **Performance** — Fast loading times benefit all users, especially those on slower connections or mobile networks

---

## Known limitations and ongoing improvements

Accessibility is an ongoing practice, not a destination. While I've built this site with accessibility in mind, there may be areas for improvement. I regularly audit the site using:

- [WAVE Web Accessibility Evaluation Tool](https://wave.webaim.org/) by WebAIM
- Browser developer tools and accessibility inspectors
- Manual testing with keyboard navigation and screen readers
- Community feedback from users

Issues and improvements are tracked in the [GitHub repository](https://github.com/ramirobarrantes/website) for transparency and accountability.

## Resources

If you'd like to learn more about web accessibility, I recommend:

- [Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/quickref/) — The official standard
- [WebAIM](https://webaim.org/) — Practical accessibility guidance
- [The A11Y Project](https://www.a11yproject.com/) — Community-driven accessibility education
- [Inclusive Components](https://inclusive-components.design/) — Design patterns that work for everyone
